_comment: 1965 Ford Mustang convertible, 289 four-barrel V8 (210 hp, early 1965), Ford four-speed, 3.00 axle, 6.50-14 bias-ply tyres, manual steering, drum brakes. Model: Sketchfab 1965 Ford Mustang Convertible by kristian123 (CC BY 4.0).
name: 1965 Mustang 289

sources.driver_eye: Eye 1.03 m up: the 1965 Mustang's upright seat and 51 in roof put a seated driver's eye near 1.03-1.05 m (owner's playtest: 0.97 sat too low).
sources.tyre_tmeasy: TMeasy with a bias-ply side curve (estimate: 9.5 per rad, peak slip 0.21). Grip fitted by scripts/fit-tyres.ps1 to Car Life's 264 ft 70-0 and 0.70 g skidpad; the drive peak (tmeasy_peak_mu_x 0.95, above the braking fit's 0.912) is fitted to the same test's 8.9 s 0-60, which is launch-limited on these tyres.
sources.calibration: 0-60 mph 8.9 s: Car Life, 289/210 hp four-speed (table at musclecarfacts.com/ford-mustang/337-1965-mustang); Road & Track's 210 hp four-speed: about 9 s, 16.5 s quarter mile (auto.howstuffworks.com/1965-1966-ford-mustang.htm). 70-0 mph 264 ft derived from Car Life's measured 20 ft/s2 (0.62 g) from 80 mph, drums with rear lock-up (tunnelram.net reprint of the 1965 Car Life Mustang special).
sources.engine: 289 four-barrel: 210 bhp at 4400 rpm, 300 lb-ft at 2800 rpm (early 1965; 225 bhp / 305 lb-ft after the mid-year revision), per Car Life 1965; curve shape estimated.
sources.gearing: Ford four-speed wide ratios 2.78/1.93/1.36/1.00 (third gear 1.36 per Car Life), 3.00 axle per the Car Life test car.
sources.chassis: 108 in wheelbase, 55.4/56 in track, 181.6 in long (Ford specifications via VIN decode); rear share under 45 % (Car Life); 21.7:1 manual steering, 3.73 turns.
sources.estimates: Mass (convertible V8 about 2,890 lb), centre of gravity, inertia, spring rates (about 1.15/1.3 Hz), dampers, brake torques, tyre grip and the 0.70 g skidpad target (no period skidpad test found).

calibration_open: Skidpad target 0.70 g is an estimate for 1965 bias-ply tyres, not a measurement. Brake-in-turn: with 4-wheel drums and no proportioning valve the car spins at 0.8-1.0 pedal in a 0.5 g bend once the rears lock after the fronts; period-true for a drum-braked 1965 car, not checked against a measured test.

card.handling: Car Life (1965): understeer minimal and handling near neutral; too much throttle brings oversteer. Slow manual steering, 3.73 turns lock to lock.
card.sources: Turning circle 11.6 m (38.1 ft): autoevolution and auto-data.net 1965 Mustang 289 listings. Steering 21.7:1 manual, 3.73 turns: Car Life 1965 (car file). Handling: Car Life 1965 Mustang road test reprint (tunnelram.net).
